author: IGN
description:
In today's Daily Fix:
It's been almost nothing but bad news for Xbox and its subsidiaries ever since CEO Asha Sharma announced the great and terrible Xbox reset of 2026. But there is some silver lining to all of the chaos: Bethesda Studios head Todd Howard has announced a roadmap for the company's IP including Fallout, The Elder Scrolls, and Starfield. Confirmed are remakes of Fallout 3 and New Vegas, and the next mainline game, Fallout 5, is in development. But right now their biggest priority is The Elder Scrolls 6, which we've seen nothing of save for a teaser trailer back in 2018. In other gaming adjacent news, the God of War live-action series encountered a major setback when star Ryan Hurst suffered a torn bicep and will need to be recast. Apparently the recovery time will be too long and his 12-year-old co-star Callum Vinson will likely have aged noticeably enough for the footage not to match. And finally, we have this week's latest gaming releases.
title: Plans for Fallout, Elder Scrolls, More Revealed in Bethesda Studios Roadmap - IGN Daily Fix

author: IGN
description:
For decades, borrowing and sharing video games has been a fundamental part of the gaming experience, but that reality is rapidly slipping away. With Sony deciding to end physical disc production in January 2028, while PlayStation 6 and Xbox’s Project Helix are reportedly dropping disc drives altogether, the industry is accelerating toward a digital-only future where true ownership is replaced by Digital Rights Management: effectively a long-term loan that publishers can revoke at any moment. For various reasons, sometimes legal, sometimes financial, this reality has already sent beloved titles like Spec Ops: The Line, Deadpool, and Super Mario Maker into near-extinction.

The death of the physical disc doesn't just impact your shelf; it threatens to destroy the entire second-hand market ecosystem built around retailers like GameStop and CEX. However, a digital future doesn't have to mean the end of player autonomy. By looking toward anti-DRM storefronts like Good Old Games (GOG), pion
title: Owning Your Games Has Become More Important Than Ever

author: IGN
description: Welcome back to Next-Gen Console Watch! This Daemon is joined by Ryan McCaffrey from Podcast Unlocked, and Brian Altano from Beyond! to discuss the continued criticism they've faced since announcing the end of physical game media production. The fans have been letting them know how they feel in the comments of every YouTube video and social media post made since the announcement. But despite the anger, Sony will likely stay the course, and will stop producing games on disc in 2028. And though gamers may gain shelf space, they lose in something more intangible. Plus we have last week's poll results, and a new poll for you to vote on at IGN.com and Spotify.
title: PlayStation’s Physical Game Problem Isn’t Going Away - Next-Gen Console Watch
